summary:
NASA-FLAME is a full-stack, AI-powered microgravity combustion research platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It focuses on understanding how flames behave in space, where the absence of normal gravity changes combustion patterns, flame shapes, heat distribution, and fuel behaviour.
On Earth, gravity causes hot gases to rise through natural convection, creating familiar flame shapes. In microgravity, this effect is significantly reduced, causing flames to behave differently and sometimes form nearly spherical structures. Understanding these differences is important for improving spacecraft fire safety and designing safer space missions.
Our solution combines a web-based research platform, backend APIs, scientific datasets, AI-powered analysis, and flame simulation capabilities. Users can explore combustion parameters, examine flame behaviour, compare experimental and simulated results, and understand how different conditions influence combustion in microgravity.
The platform uses a modern Next.js frontend and FastAPI backend, supported by a structured database and AI/ML components. It also references NASA combustion research, including ACME, FLEX, and other microgravity experiments.
Our goal: Make complex microgravity combustion research easier to explore, analyse, and understand while supporting safer future space exploration.
details:
NASA-FLAME: Fire Beyond Gravity

NASA-FLAME is an AI-powered microgravity combustion research platform designed to help users explore and understand how flames behave in space. On Earth, gravity drives natural convection, causing hot gases to rise and flames to take their familiar shape. In microgravity, this effect is significantly reduced, resulting in unusual flame shapes, heat distribution, and combustion behaviour. Understanding these differences is essential for improving fire safety aboard spacecraft and supporting future space exploration.

Our platform brings together scientific research, data analysis, and simulation capabilities in one interactive web application. Users can explore combustion parameters, examine flame behaviour under different conditions, compare experimental and simulated results, and understand how environmental factors influence microgravity combustion. AI-powered analysis helps interpret patterns and provides insights into combustion behaviour.

The project aims to make complex scientific information more accessible, support combustion research, and contribute to safer spacecraft design and fire prevention strategies.

We developed the platform using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, and a structured database, alongside AI/ML components and scientific data-processing tools. We also referenced NASA research and microgravity combustion investigations, including ACME and FLEX.

The creative aspect of NASA-FLAME is its integration of research, interactive visualisation, AI-driven insights, and simulation into a unified platform rather than presenting scientific information as static reports.

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, data provenance, usability, accessibility, performance, scalability, and the practical challenges of analysing combustion in microgravity.

Our intended impact is to make microgravity combustion research easier to understand and explore while contributing to the broader goal of safer human spaceflight.
